title: Articles 32 and 226 Compared — PIL Forum Choice

content.overview: PIL forum choice turns on Articles 32 and 226: Supreme Court Part III enforcement versus High Court jurisdiction over fundamental rights and other legal rights within territorial limits. Liberal standing applies in both; subject-matter and territory differ.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Part III only or other legal rights too? (2) National vs regional scale? (3) Territorial link to a High Court? (4) Bona fides? (5) Abuse filters?
content.study:
Core comparison: Article 32 — Supreme Court, fundamental rights, itself a fundamental right. Article 226 — High Courts, fundamental rights and other legal rights for any other purpose, territorial competence.

PIL uses both with liberalised standing. Choose 32 when Supreme Court Part III enforcement is fit; choose 226 for regional wrongs, other legal rights, or first High Court forum.

Aligned with thin topics art-32 and art-226. Case-law verification remains separate.

sections.heading: Article 32 in PIL
sections.body: Supreme Court gateway limited to enforcement of fundamental rights; liberal standing within that limit.

sections.heading: Article 226 in PIL
sections.body: High Court gateway for fundamental and other legal rights; territorial limits bind.

sections.heading: Forum-choice factors
sections.body: Rights base, scale of injury, territorial link, urgency, and appropriate hierarchy.

sections.heading: Shared limits
sections.body: Bona fides, private-dispute filters, and costs apply under both articles.

sections.heading: Not interchangeable labels
sections.body: The PIL label does not make 32 and 226 the same court or the same rights base.

examples.title: National Part III claim
examples.body: Systemic fundamental-rights violation of national scale — consider Article 32.

examples.title: District statutory duty
examples.body: Local public-duty default with territorial link — consider Article 226.

hypotheticals.question: Is every PIL better filed under Article 32?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Forum depends on rights base, scale, and territory; 226 is often the proper first forum.

distinctions.title: Article 32 vs Article 226
distinctions.left: Supreme Court; Part III; fundamental right to move SC.
distinctions.right: High Courts; fundamental + other legal rights; territory.

misconceptions.trap: 32 and 226 are the same for every PIL.
misconceptions.correction: They differ in court, rights, and territory.
